title: Customer Network Onboarding Heuristic Playbook (PRD Notes)
content:
Purpose:
A concise playbook-style PRD capturing heuristics and UX patterns for onboarding customer-managed networking into Redwood Private. Focus is on a minimalist audit surface, deterministic approval gates, and fast operator workflows that keep customer control while providing Redwood necessary observability for support and compliance.

Problem statement (short):
Customers onboarding their VPCs (or on-prem edges) struggle with long handoffs: ambiguous log formats, too many approval steps, and lack of clear evidence bundles for post-change forensics. This increases time-to-first-request and creates support escalations. We need a pragmatic set of rules and a lightweight evidence format that operators can validate quickly and that auditors can query.

Goals (MUST):
- Define a minimal evidence bundle for onboarding/changes that satisfies typical enterprise auditors (timestamped change record, operator assertion, config checksum, connectivity proof).
- Design approval gate heuristics that can be auto-evaluated by the control plane with clear human-explainable failures.
- Provide UX flow for customers and operators so initial handoff completes within 24-48 hours for standard cases, and within 2 weeks for custom network topologies.
- Define telemetry and retention policies for audit logs to support 90-day investigations by default with configurable longer retention for enterprise customers.

Non-goals:
- We are NOT building a full SIEM integration in v1 (we will provide export hooks and compact evidence format).
- We will not attempt to normalize every vendor NAT/Gateway log format; instead we rely on a validated handshake/connection test and optional connector adapters later.

Personas:
- Platform Operator (customer): performs the network change, runs tests, uploads evidence, expects a fast and predictable approval flow.
- Redwood Edge Operator (support): validates evidence, triages failures, may request additional samples.
- Security/Audit reviewer (customer or third party): needs readable, tamper-evident records to prove change intent and execution.

User Journey (happy path):
1) Customer triggers onboarding flow in Console -> provides VPC metadata, contact info, and desired egress rules.
2) Console shows pre-checks and generates a unique onboarding change-id.
3) Customer runs an automated verifier (agentless curl/webhook-based) that posts back a short signed report to Redwood with connectivity snapshots and a config checksum.
4) Redwood control plane evaluates heuristics (checksum match, connectivity, cross-account access rules) and either auto-approves or opens a single approval ticket.
5) When auto-approved, operator gets email + console confirmation; audit record is stored and exportable.

Heuristic Approval Gate (summary):
- Gate A: Identity & Access sanity -> required keys, customer admin assertion, and aws/iam principal match.
- Gate B: Minimal network safety -> no 0.0.0.0/0 in inbound rules for control-plane-sensitive ports; egress caps for telemetry endpoints.
- Gate C: Proof-of-connectivity -> signed connection test to control plane and one successful webhook roundtrip.
- Gate D: Evidence completeness -> presence of config checksum, operator assertion (signed), and at least one encrypted snapshot.

Each gate returns a short failure code and user-facing remediation link. The control plane applies a simple allowlist of auto-approve patterns (common CIDR ranges, known partner ASNs, recent customer attestations).

Evidence bundle (minimal):
- change_id: human readable id (e.g., cust-0422-onboard-3)
- operator_assertion: free-text + signer_name + signer_email + timestamp
- config_checksum: sha256 of exported VPC route/security manifest
- connectivity_proof: signed timestamped request/response sample (base64) showing control-plane endpoint reachability
- short_diff: optional minimal diff vs previously recorded manifest (if any)
- signature_meta: algorithm (rsa-pss/ed25519), verifier hints
- retention_hint: default 90 days, customer can request longer via contract

Log & Telemetry plan (v1):
- Audit logs recorded as compact JSON lines into immutable store with fields: change_id, gate_statuses (codes), signer_id, control_plane_node, ip_whitelist_hash, retention_until.
- Sample retention policy: default 90 days; alerts for retention nearing expiry sent to both parties at 14/7/1 day markers.
- Search & export: support CSV/JSON export by change_id or customer_id; Confluence/PRD will call out future GraphQL index for richer queries.

Operator UX & Runbook (support):
- Triage view shows the first failing gate, most recent connectivity sample, and a one-click request for additional evidence (example: run remote traceroute).
- Quick escalation button creates a secure ephemeral workspace linking evidence bundle + Slack channel with customer and SRE rotation.
- If a gate repeatedly times out, playbook recommends either remote debugging session or rollback of recently applied rules.

Security & tamper resistance:
- Evidence bundles include signer metadata and support detached signatures (customer can sign locally).
- Control-plane stores only signed artifacts and immutable metadata hashes; raw artifacts are encrypted-in-transit and at-rest using KMS.
- For critical changes we surface an attestation chain with optional HSM-signed receipts (enterprise add-on).

Acceptance criteria (for v1 beta):
- 70% of standard onboarding attempts auto-approve under the heuristic rules in internal pilot across 10 customers.
- Support time-to-first-successful-request median <= 36 hours for auto-approve; <= 10 days for fallback manual workflows.
- Audit bundle format validated by Security and legal for typical compliance checklists (SOC2 infra control subset).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: False negatives blocking safe networks -> mitigation: provide clear remediation steps and small set of emergency bypass rules with manual SRE approval and audit.
- Risk: Evidence format not accepted by some customers -> mitigation: export hooks and a small SDK to generate validator-friendly bundles.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): implement proof-of-connectivity agentless verifier, basic gate evaluator, and immutable audit log store. Internal iteration with infra team.
- Phase 1 (pilot): invite 5 customers (existing Private customers) to test onboarding playbook; collect telemetry and refine heuristics.
- Phase 2 (open beta): expose Console flow to all Private customers with opt-in telemetry. Add short support SLA for onboarding.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require customer-side detached signatures in v1 or keep signer as email+otp? (security favors detached signatures; UX favors email OTP).
- Retention pricing model: should extended retention be an add-on or tiered as part of Dedicated contracts?
- Do we need a small agent for environments where webhook egress is blocked? (agent increases complexity but improves reliability).

Next steps / owner action items:
- Leah: prototype control-plane gate evaluator and sample audit line format (PD-1209).
- Marco: draft operator triage UI mockups and Slack escalation layout (due 2025-11-16).
- Priya: legal review of evidence bundle for SOC2 and EU DPA constraints (due 2025-11-20).
- Owen: reach out to three pilot customers to scope typical onboarding manifests and collect sample configs.

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments (working doc style):
- Consider a short human-readable summary attached to bundles for faster auditor review ("what changed in one sentence").
- Could use a single HMAC seed for short-term ephemeral verification to reduce friction, then swap to detached signatures for long-term retention.
- Keep export minimal: avoid dumping raw flow logs; prefer curated snapshots + checksums to reduce retention cost.
- Keep list of failure reasons short and machine-friendly (e.g., GATE_CONN_TIMEOUT, GATE_CFG_MISMATCH, GATE_IAM_MISMATCH).

References & links:
- CONFLUENCE:PD-452-onboarding-patterns (existing onboarding patterns research)
- JIRA:PD-1209 (proto evaluator task)
- github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/88 (early verifier script)

End of doc.
